trace_name: Upper GI endoscopy: ongoing hematemesis, sedation before airway protection

errors.detail: sedation administered (m1.2) in ongoing hematemesis before the airway was protected (microstep m1.3 not performed): sedation suppresses the protective airway reflexes over a stomach full of blood, and the sedation standard's rescue and anesthesia-assistance provisions exist for exactly this configuration (T53)

complications.detail: aspiration of gastric blood computed at the sedation act: a named sedation-related cardiopulmonary adverse event (T52), in the event class that forms the largest share of this procedure's adverse events (structural outcome; no gas-exchange trajectory is computed)

description: [t=60s] m0.1: Review the indication and assess hemodynamic status immediately: acute upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage confirmed as the presentation; where hemodynamic instability exists, prompt intravascular volume replacement is begun, initially with crystalloid fluids, before any endoscopy is contemplated (T49, statement 1, strong recommendation)

[t=120s] m0.2: Pre-endoscopy risk stratification with the Glasgow–Blatchford Score: computed from the presentation's clinical and laboratory parameters; a score of 0–1 identifies the very-low-risk patient who can be managed as an outpatient, and this admitted bleeding patient is stratified above that line (T49, statement 4 / Main Recommendation 1, strong recommendation)

[t=180s] m0.3: Transfusion strategy set before the procedure: a restrictive red-cell strategy — transfusion prompted at a hemoglobin threshold of ≤ 7 g/dL with a post-transfusion target of 7–9 g/dL, or ≤ 8 g/dL targeting ≥ 10 g/dL where acute or chronic cardiovascular disease stands (T49, statements 2–3, strong recommendations)

[t=240s] m0.4: Consent review and team brief: perforation (≤ 0.03% at diagnostic endoscopy, rising with therapy, T52), sedation-related cardiopulmonary events (T52, T53), the rebleeding rates by Forrest class that the findings may carry (55% Ia/Ib and 43% IIa untreated, T51), and the escalation sequence if hemostasis fails or bleeding recurs — repeat endoscopy, then transcatheter embolization, then surgery (T49, T50) — stated aloud
[t=300s] m0.5: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist: Sign In

[t=360s] m0.6: Antithrombotic and culprit-drug review: antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy identified with a resumption plan recorded — anticoagulation resumed as soon as bleeding is controlled, preferably within or soon after 7 days, on thromboembolic risk (T49); any culprit NSAID identified for the cause-directed plan at m7.3
[t=420s] m0.7: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist: Time Out

[t=480s] m0.8: Timing set: endoscopy is performed early — within 24 hours of presentation, following hemodynamic resuscitation; urgent (≤ 12 h) endoscopy is not pursued as a routine, patient outcomes not being improved by it (T49, Main Recommendations 3–4; T50)
[t=540s] dp1 -> proceed-endoscopy

[t=600s] m1.1: Airway and aspiration-risk assessment: hematemesis and gastric blood load, consciousness level, comorbidity and airway anatomy assessed, and the sedation plan chosen against that assessment — the assessment the dp2 decision is taken on (T53)
[t=660s] dp2 -> moderate-sedation-monitored

[t=720s] m1.2: Sedation or anesthesia administered to the planned depth with the full monitoring set running: pulse oximetry, electrocardiography and intermittent blood pressure measurement, supplemental oxygen, capnography considered and available for deep sedation, and trained personnel dedicated to monitoring who can rescue a patient who becomes unresponsive or unable to protect the airway (T53). This act IS the airway–sedation account (crit3): monitoring demonstrates the account; it does not substitute for the protection the assessed risk demands

[t=720s] err.unprotected-airway: sedation administered (m1.2) in ongoing hematemesis before the airway was protected (microstep m1.3 not performed): sedation suppresses the protective airway reflexes over a stomach full of blood, and the sedation standard's rescue and anesthesia-assistance provisions exist for exactly this configuration (T53)
[t=720s] aspiration computed: sedation over an unprotected airway in ongoing hematemesis

[t=780s] m1.3: Airway protection: general anesthesia induced and the trachea intubated before instrumentation, securing the airway against aspiration of gastric blood for the therapeutic procedure (T53: anesthesia assistance for high-risk, prolonged and therapeutic cases; T52: aspiration among the sedation-related adverse events). Required in the ongoing-hematemesis configuration, where the scenario inserts it into the attempt's required set; elective elsewhere
[t=840s] help called: anaesthesia senior help

[t=900s] m1.4: Bite block placed and the gastroscope passed under direct vision through the oesophagus into the stomach: no blind advancement, and no advancement against resistance — the perforation discipline of the instrument (T52)

[t=960s] m2.1: Oesophagus surveyed on passage: varices and a Mallory-Weiss tear sought and excluded by inspection — both are outside this nonvariceal procedure's remit (varices end it via the dp1 bailout; the tear is a named non-variant), and neither is treated under this gate (T49, scope)

[t=1020s] m2.2: Gastric survey: the stomach examined in full, including the retroflexed view of the fundus and cardia; retained blood and clot cleared by irrigation and suction so the mucosa is actually seen — an unexamined gastric pool is where a proximal lesser-curvature lesion hides (T54)

[t=1080s] m2.3: Duodenal survey: bulb and second part examined; the posterior bulb wall — the gastroduodenal artery's territory, and the wall whose ulcer erodes it — inspected deliberately, not in passing (T49; T51)

[t=1140s] m3.1: Bleeding source identified and localised: the culprit lesion seen and its site recorded — organ, wall and size — with the surveyed territory accounted for, so the lesion therapy will address is the lesion that is bleeding (crit1) (T49)

[t=1200s] m3.2: Lesion classified by its Forrest stigmata before any therapy: spurting (Ia), oozing (Ib), nonbleeding visible vessel (IIa), adherent clot (IIb), flat pigmented spot (IIc) or clean base (III) — the classification is to be used in all patients with peptic ulcer hemorrhage, because therapy keys on it (crit2) (T49; T51)
[t=1200s] Identification and Forrest classification before therapy achieved: all three criteria demonstrated
[t=1260s] dp3 -> forrest-iia

[t=1320s] m4.1: Pre-therapy pause: the declared classification is restated aloud and the therapy plan matched to it in the team's hearing — the modality set the class dictates, epinephrine never standing alone for a high-risk lesion (T49; T50) — and the rescue pathway (cap-mounted clip or topical hemostatic for refractory bleeding, T49; TAE and surgical cover beyond it) is confirmed available before the first therapy act

[t=1380s] m4.2: Second look at the lesion before therapy: the base washed and the stigmata re-confirmed at close inspection; if washing changes the class — a clot lifting to show a vessel, a spot washing clean — the declaration at dp3 is corrected before therapy, never after it (T49; T51)

[t=1440s] m5.2: Epinephrine injection: dilute epinephrine injected into and around the lesion for tamponade and vasoconstriction — a temporising modality that buys the field for definitive therapy and is never the whole of it: epinephrine injection is not used as monotherapy (T49, strong recommendation; T50, statement 10)

[t=1500s] m5.3: Mechanical therapy: through-the-scope clips applied across the vessel or lesion, occluding it directly — with epinephrine for the actively bleeding classes (T49, Main Recommendation 5), a definitive modality alone or combined for a visible vessel (T49, Main Recommendation 6; T50), and the effective modality for a Dieulafoy lesion (T54)
[t=1560s] m6.1: Hemostasis confirmed: the treated lesion observed under irrigation and over time, dry, with no ongoing bleeding from the treated site before the scope moves on (T49; T50)

[t=1620s] m6.2: Completion survey: the surveyed territory re-examined for a second lesion before withdrawal — a bleeding admission can hold more than one lesion, and the treated one is not assumed to be the only one; in the Dieulafoy configuration this survey is where the unsearched-for artery declares the miss (T49; T54)

[t=1680s] m7.1: High-dose proton pump inhibitor therapy after endoscopic hemostasis: 80 mg intravenous bolus then 8 mg/h infusion for 72 hours (T49); high-dose PPI, continuously or intermittently, for 3 days after successful hemostasis of high-risk stigmata (T50) — and likewise for adherent-clot stigmata not treated endoscopically (T49)

[t=1740s] m7.2: Monitored setting with rebleeding surveillance: serial observations and hemoglobin through the high-risk rebleeding window, the team knowing the untreated-risk figures the lesion's class carries even after therapy (T51) and the plan at dp4 if bleeding declares

[t=1800s] m7.3: Cause-directed plan recorded: the culprit drug stopped where one stands (the NSAID of the index presentation among them), the indication reviewed, and any interrupted antithrombotic therapy's resumption timed on thromboembolic risk (T49)

[t=1860s] m7.4: Rebleeding plan stated and handed over: on clinical evidence of rebleeding — repeat endoscopy with therapy first, a cap-mounted clip considered; after a failed second attempt, transcatheter embolization; surgery when embolization is unavailable or has failed (T49) — and NO routine second-look endoscopy is booked: scheduled re-examination without rebleeding is not recommended (T49, Main Recommendation 13)

[t=1920s] m8.1: Findings and therapy documented: the lesion, its site, the Forrest class as declared, the modalities delivered, and the hemostasis result — the record the rebleeding plan and any repeat procedure key on (T49)
[t=1980s] m8.2: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist: Sign Out

[t=2040s] m8.3: Disposition set: monitored admission for treated and high-risk lesions; discharge reserved for the very-low-risk pathway — Glasgow–Blatchford ≤ 1, or low-risk stigmata with stability — with the recurrent-bleeding warning given (T49)
[t=2100s] complication recognised: aspiration
plus: The gate was demonstrated before the first therapy act — source identified and localised, lesion Forrest-classified and declared, airway–sedation account made: the classification is to be used in all peptic ulcer hemorrhage because therapy keys on it (T49).
Pre-therapy pause performed: the declared classification was restated and the modality set matched to it with the team before the first therapy act (T49; T50).
All three WHO checklist phases were completed at their integration points (T6).
delta: err.unprotected-airway — sedation administered (m1.2) in ongoing hematemesis before the airway was protected (microstep m1.3 not performed): sedation suppresses the protective airway reflexes over a stomach full of blood, and the sedation standard's rescue and anesthesia-assistance provisions exist for exactly this configuration (T53)
directive: In ongoing hematemesis the airway is the first procedure: protect it before sedation depth, because sedation removes the reflexes that are keeping blood out of the trachea, and aspiration is among this procedure's commonest serious adverse events (T52; T53).
summary: Verdict: PASS (formative only — no construct evidence exists for these scores yet).
Checklist 100.0% (28/28), safety gate 4/4, process 4/5, physiology 7/7, management 5/5.
